decisive_metrics.all_three_generated_the_same_invalid_tem: <task_relevance_map> The uncertainty-aware planning stance is high; its strongest region is CAM_FRONT_LEFT/middle_left; its temporal trend is rising.

interpretation: The explicit relevance map and K-ranking objectives are learnable, but the current single-pass VLM does not reliably route their result into language generation.
A matched full-answer preference loss does not solve the bottleneck: the model collapses onto an observation-semantics template and still prefers the maintain answer under on-path UQ.
This is an architectural communication failure between R/K and language, not evidence that more repetitions of the same one-event objective will help.

next_architecture.name: two_pass_task_risk_language_bridge_v1
next_architecture.pass_1: Use route-conditioned, view/space-aligned neutral query tokens with ORION visual tokens to predict task relevance R. The current U magnitude must not define R.
next_architecture.fusion: Compute K = U * sigmoid(R) and summarize it into six view tokens plus one global task-risk token with continuous spatial statistics.
next_architecture.pass_2: Append the seven bridge tokens to the original ORION visual and spatial-UQ tokens for QA loss, matched answer preference, and deterministic free generation.
next_architecture.responsibility_boundary: Stage1 adapter still predicts only task-agnostic observation uncertainty U; the ORION/VLM relevance pass predicts R; the bridge communicates K to the VLM but does not issue brake, steering, or a hard governor command.

next_gpu_run_requires: bridge tensor-shape and finite-gradient unit tests

claim_boundary: One-event engineering diagnosis only; no held-out generalization, trajectory, closed-loop, or safety claim.
